description_full: The Vita Coco Company, Inc. develops, manufactures, markets, and distributes coconut water products under the Vita Coco brand name in the United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. It offers coconut water, oil, and juice products; Vita Coco Treats, a plant-based dairy alternative; Vita Coco Pressed, Vita Coco Coconut Juice, and Farmers Organic; Vita Coco Coconut MLK; and PWR LIFT, a protein-infused fitness drink. The company also supplies private label products to retailers. It distributes its products through club, food, drug, mass, convenience, e-commerce, and foodservice channels. The Vita Coco Company, Inc. has a strategic alliance with Homesick Turn Sweet Sips to develop fragranced candles. The company was formerly known as All Market Inc. and changed its name to The Vita Coco Company, Inc. in September 2021. The Vita Coco Company, Inc. was incorporated in 2004 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

financial_summary: The Vita Coco Company, Inc. is a mid-cap consumer defensive business with a $3.6B market cap on $610M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +13% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 48% against a 10% cost of capital — a 38-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 37%.

The business throws off $39M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.66×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.3%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 8.7% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
